finding: 94 percent of the per-token byte surplus is one mechanism: reading lm_head as f32 and paying a widen tax on native tensors. It is also the second-largest time bucket.
arithmetic: lm_head 3.81 + widen tax 2.53 = 6.34 GB, which is 93.8 percent of the 6.76 GB surplus.
corroboration: final_head_and_sampling is 634.5 ms of a 2,339 ms token, 27.1 percent. The same mechanism dominates both the byte surplus and the second-largest time bucket.

honest_gap.measured_by_category: 0.00 GB -- the record_active_bytes_for hooks are present but NOT wired into the executed decode path, so the category split above is STATIC, derived from artifact headers and an access schedule, not measured.
honest_gap.unaccounted: 1.12 GB of the measured 10.46 GB remains unexplained by the static schedule and is recorded as such rather than distributed.

why_this_is_actionable_anyway: The static schedule is derived from real artifact header sizes and a real access pattern, and its total (9.34 GB) lands within 11 percent of the measured 10.46 GB. The lm_head term is not an estimate -- 1.90 GB bf16 widened to f32 is 3.81 GB by definition, and the ledger independently shows the head bucket at 27.1 percent of time.
